21: Bengal Army: biggest, upper-caste sepoys from Awadh and Bihar, Indians far outnumber British. Sepoy is a peasant in uniform: low pay, called Suar, stuck at Subedar, 60 to 70 rupees.
1856: pay cut, no allowance for far service (money and caste loss). Awadh annexed. Widows' Remarriage Act. Canning 56-62: Mughals only 'Princes'.
New Enfield cartridge greased with cow and pig fat, bitten before loading. Bone dust rumours, missionaries since 1813. Sepoys fear attack on faith. Cartridge was only the trigger.
29 March 1857: Mangal Pandey, 34th BNI, fires; hanged 8 April. 10 May Meerut, 11 May Delhi: Bahadur Shah Zafar 37-57 proclaimed Emperor; held till 20 September. British monopoly of violence broken.

Lapse and annexation ruined rulers; Mahalwari ruined taluqdars; revenue and moneylenders ruined peasants; British goods ruined artisans. All feared for religion: 1813, Sati 1829, Lex Loci 1850, Widows 1856.
Nana Sahib Kanpur, Hazrat Mahal Lucknow, Lakshmi Bai Jhansi, Kunwar Singh Jagdishpur, Zafar Delhi, Tantia Tope guerrilla. Lakshmi Bai dies June 1858; Tope hanged April 1859; Zafar dies 1862.
Rebels: no money, weapons or central command. All sepoys went to Delhi, so Delhi's fall was the revolt's fall. No telegraph; Bombay and Madras quiet; Punjabis and Gurkhas helped British.

Colonial view: sepoy mutiny. Savarkar (1909) and Marx: war of independence. Mainstream: more than a mutiny, but no modern nationalism. Against: Scam B areas, no manifesto. For: common enemy, Hindu-Muslim unity.
GOI Act 1858 ends EIC: Queen Victoria sovereign, Secretary of State. 1 November 1858 Proclamation: tolerance, no more annexations, British India 63%. Indians seen as inferior; harsher rule.
Canning 56-62: Police Commission 1860, Police Act March 1861, Indians kept out of key posts. Exam in London, age 19 to 23; Lytton 76-80's Statutory Civil Service takes chosen elites.
Peel Commission (July 1858, report March 1859), European Forces (India) Act 1860. Ratios 1:2 Bengal, 1:3 Madras and Bombay; no Indian artillery. Mixed regiments, martial races, kept in barracks.
WEMC, taught British liberalism, wanted a share and was locked out. That anger seeded the modern nationalist INM; by 1929 Purna Swaraj. 1857 was the hinge.
22: After 1857 peasants went to court and organised, using colonial law against colonial rule. The WEMC spoke for the ryot in press, courts, associations. Courts, press, peaceful protest come first.
1788: EIC loans to ten European planters. Nij cost too much, so Ryoti: lease from zamindars, contract ryots to grow indigo on 25% of land, with loans and seed drills.
Indigo ruined soil, price not paying, ryot borrowed to repay loans. Stock Exchange crisis cut prices; a sympathetic Lieutenant Governor told Collectors to side with ryots.
Ryots refused loans and indigo, boycotted planters' agents, withheld rent when sued. On eviction they organised and went to court under the Rent Act of 1859: Non-Cooperation before Gandhi.
DeenBandhu Mitra's Neel Darpan (1860): Datta translated, James Long published; Long fined Rs 1,000 (Kaliprasanna Sinha paid), jailed a month. Hindu Patriot, Somprakash and BrIA (1851) backed ryots.
Indigo Commission (1860): honour old contracts, refuse new. By 1863 Tinkathia in Bihar (3/20th). BASF synthetic indigo 1897 (Prelims 2020) killed it; Champaran (1917), Act 1918 ended Tinkathia.

Zamindars broke Rent Act 1859 rights: illegal rents, Abwabs. Ryots formed Agrarian Leagues (Ishan Chandra Roy); WEMC split. Ripon 80-84's Rent Commission (1880), Tenancy Act 1885: rights after 12 years.

No-tax 1873-74. Limitation Law 1859 allowed 3 years' interest, so moneylenders made fresh bonds. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870): 17,000 signatures. 1875: ryots burned bonds, not lives. Relief Act 1879.

Namdhari (Kuka) sect, Baba Ram Singh, exiled to Burma 1872 (not imp). 1907 canal colony bill: Lahore Indian Association, Arya Samaj, Singh Sabha; British withdrew it, fearing the Punjab-recruited Army.
Peasants organised, used colonial law, found WEMC voice. Not yet the national movement but its soil: non-cooperation, no-tax, boycott, legal challenge, all rehearsed before Champaran (1917).
23: First voice: educated landed class. BrIA 1851 (Radhakanta Deb), Bombay Association and Madras Native Association 1852: three petitions on Charter Act 1853. Never against rule: exploitation 'un-British'.
Nothing granted. Landlords had too much to lose: Permanent Settlement 1793, police protection. Teacher: Of, By, For the landed class, not the people.
After 1857 Western education makes the WEMC, meant as loyal Brown Sahibs. No power-sharing, so admiration turns to demand for rights. Uneven (1921 literacy 8%): starts in Calcutta, Bombay, Madras.
By 1875 over 400 newspapers, 1.5 lakh readers make regional leaders national. Railways and telegraph from the 1850s let leaders meet. Empire's infrastructure becomes anti-colonial.
1850 Black Acts suspended after 'white rebellion'. Lex Loci Act 1850 over Indian opposition. Income Tax (1860, 1868) in famines: 'No Taxation Without Representation'. 1870 education budget cut.
Lytton 76-80: ICS age 19 (1876), Delhi Durbar (1877) in famine, Vernacular Press Act and Arms Act (1878), Statutory Civil Service, Second Afghan War (1878-80).
Gladstone's Liberals win 1880, send Ripon 80-84: Tenancy Act 1885, Factories Act 1881, VPA repealed, Arms Act amended, ICS age 21, Local Self-Government 1882. Simultaneous exam fails.
Law Member C.P. Ilbert: Indian district judges may try Britons. Europeans protest; bill withdrawn, mixed jury. WEMC's last doubt gone: Britain will not treat Indians as equals.
Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870, Ranade), Commons petition 1875. Surendranath Banerjee founds Indian Association (1876); Lahore 1877; Madras Mahajan Sabha 1884. Of and by WEMC, for all the people.
New bodies lead peasants (Indigo 1859-63, Deccan 1875, Canal Colony 1907), run famine relief, protest Plantation Labour Act 1859, demand Council seats. After Councils Act 1892 they use the Councils.
Western education, free press, racial provocation, WEMC associations, railways and telegraphs meet in the Indian National Congress, Bombay 1885: first all-India party.
24: Regional bodies protested Lex Loci Act 1850, Income Tax 1868, for Indianisation (1877), against Afghan War and Vernacular Press Act (1878), for Ilbert Bill (1883-84). None met.

British India Association 1851 tried a joint petition. Native Press Association 1877, Banerjea President. Indian Association (1876) launched Conference 1883; Theosophical convention 1884; National Fund 1885.
A.O. Hume, Liberal retired civil servant: Mayo 69-72 (1871), dismissed over Lytton 76-80's Afghan War spending, backed Ripon 80-84. Wanted INC as 'His Majesty's Opposition'.
INC founded Bombay, December 1885, W.C. Bonnerjee 1st President. 1st all India ORG but not all Indian: founder a Briton. Hume General Secretary, never President.
Naoroji 1886, Tyabji 1887 (1st Muslim), Yule 1888 (1st non-Indian), Wedderburn 1889 and 1910, Webb 1894, Besant 1917 (1st woman), Das 1922 (prison), Naidu 1925. Tyabji died August 1906.
Wedderburn's 1913 biography: Hume got seven volumes of secret reports in 1878, met Dufferin 84-88, and they founded INC as safety valve. Teacher: pressure cooker, INC the whistle.
Seven volumes never found; only source a friend's book four decades later. Dufferin 84-88 called Moderates 'Babus', feared Irish Home Rule League. Teacher: never in exam.
Wedderburn wrote to make friend Hume a patriot. Hume's real use: mediator for Bombay, Calcutta, Madras and protective cover (Gokhale 1913). Indians used Hume as lightning conductor.
Wedderburn: 2nd non-Indian President, Indian Parliamentary Committee 1893 with W.S. Caine. Jardine: Judge, MP 1906-1918. Yule: 1st non-Indian, 400 tigers. Webb: Irish MP, Madras 1894.
Curzon 99-05 'peaceful demise' (1998); Tyabji trap; 2000 Naidu, Das, Hume, Webb; 2004, 2008 first session; 2011 Wedderburn and Caine; 2015 firsts. Mains - No Q, PRELIMS ticked.
